title: My mother & Claude: teaching AI to a retired pharmacist, step by step
summary: Ruben walks his non-technical mom through Claude using a real task (planning an apartment succession). He shows a simple prompt formula, how to fix hallucinations with source rules, and how to turn an answer into a product. The second half is paywalled.

principles.text: Prompt with a goal, a success criterion, your context, and an invitation to ask questions.
principles.quote: I need [goal] that I will consider achieved once [success criteria]. I am [context about me, my situation]. If necessary, ask me clarifying questions first.

principles.text: Let the AI interview you so you don't fear missing details.
principles.quote: But that’s Claude’s job. That’s why we added, “If necessary, ask me clarifying questions first.”

principles.text: Beat hallucinations by restricting the AI to official domains and demanding citations.
principles.quote: you can force Claude or other AI to cite their sources and pick official ones only.

principles.text: Win AI skeptics by showing capability: documents and contracts, not just answers.
principles.quote: That’s how you expand someone’s brain about AI: they finally feel how it widens their options.

principles.text: Remove typing friction with dictation so non-typers can use AI.
principles.quote: So I showed her Wispr Flow, a dictation tool. We simply talked like she would to her notary.

principles.text: Technology can't be stopped, and the world splits between frontier-tech experts and likable people.
principles.quote: the world is dividing in two: either you’re extremely good at handling frontier technology (like AI), or you’re so likable people keep coming back to your shop
